findings.issue_text: Passing an empty update object to Prisma leaves SelectedCalendar.updatedAt unchanged, so the intended refresh does not occur
Backfilling existing calendar cache rows with NOW() incorrectly marks deployment time as their last refresh time
ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, potentially modifying or creating .env outside the repository
cleanup always exits with status 0, masking initialization and rate-limit failures as successful execution
Using BSD-specific sed -i '' fails on GNU/Linux when updating an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL
Hard-coding en-US ignores the active application locale and incorrectly formats cache timestamps for localized users

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfilling existing calendar cache rows with NOW() incorrectly marks deployment time as their last refresh time

adjudication.rationale: The migration in 20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql adds the updatedAt column with 'DEFAULT NOW()' which means all existing CalendarCache rows will have their updatedAt set to the deployment time, not their actual last refresh time. This is misleading because the UI shows 'Last updated: {{timestamp}}' based on this field, making users think old cache entries were just refreshed when they weren't. The schema.prisma also shows '@default(now())' which perpetuates this for the backfill case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, potentially modifying or creating .env outside the repository

adjudication.rationale: The script at scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh sets ENV_FILE="../.env" which is a relative path. When the script is executed, this path is resolved relative to the current working directory of the caller, not relative to the script's location. If someone runs this script from a directory other than 'scripts/', it will modify or create a .env file in an unintended location (one directory up from wherever they're running it). This is a real bug that could cause unexpected behavior or data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cleanup always exits with status 0, masking initialization and rate-limit failures as successful execution

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the script, the cleanup function always calls 'exit 0' regardless of how it was invoked. When rate-limit is hit (line 'limited to 10 tunnels per hour'), the script calls cleanup which exits with 0 instead of a non-zero error code. Similarly, if URL extraction fails, cleanup is called and exits 0. This is a real issue in the diff - the script masks failures as successes. However, this is a new test/development script (test-gcal-webhooks.sh), not production code, so while it's a valid concern about proper error handling, it's not a critical bug that would cause data loss or security issues.
